notes: Iteration-5 measures HIT-RATE over 5 trials/arm on one hard needle-in-haystack case: a type-only import of a Drizzle row type inside a vendor/shared contract (Hard rule 9, present ONLY in the new skill; verified absent from all repo docs). Fixture: 14 files, exactly one planted violation, mirror decoy (identical import shape, legal scope) plus 4 more decoy groups.

Hit-rate on the planted finding (assertion 9.1): with_skill 5/5 (100%), old_skill 5/5 (100%). NO detection delta: the old-skill agent derived the violation from the generic dependency rule (domain must not name infrastructure) — it did not need the type-only clarification, because a contract importing from modules/ is an obvious boundary crossing regardless of the `import type` nuance.

The only imperfect run: with_skill run-3 (4/5) split the single violation into two findings, separately flagging helpers.ts toReportDetailDto as a rule-5 leak — the same root cause double-counted, caught by the mirror decoy 9.2. Kept as a legitimate penalty (the prompt required reporting once, at the fix location); no assertion arbitration this iteration.

Variance: with_skill 96% +/- 8.9, old_skill 100% +/- 0. Both arms passed every decoy in every run except that one double-report — including the mirror decoy (legal import type within a module) and the service-builds-repo convention.

Conclusion across iterations 3-5: at this model tier, fixture evals cannot show a DETECTION delta for any rule the model can re-derive from first principles or repo context; deltas appear only where the skill encodes an arbitrary project-specific choice (the port-placement rule, iteration-3). The value of rules 8/9 is consistency/di-rectness of justification, not net-new detection ability.
